test_title: PYST 48: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 17 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: When was the Union Budget 2025–26 presented in Parliament by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1 February 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Budget 2025–26** was presented in the **Parliament** of India on **1 February 2025** by the Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs, **Nirmala Sitharaman**.
 
• With this presentation, **Nirmala Sitharaman** created a historical milestone by presenting her **seventh consecutive budget**, surpassing the record previously held by former Prime Minister and Finance Minister **Morarji Desai**.
 
• The budget outlines the **Government of India's** estimated receipts and expenditures for the upcoming **fiscal year**, which runs from **1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026**.
 
• Following the established tradition since **2017**, the budget was presented on the **first day of February** to ensure that the budgetary provisions and tax changes could be implemented by the start of the new financial year.
 
• The presentation was preceded by the **Economic Survey 2024-25**, which was tabled in the house on **31 January 2025**, providing a comprehensive report on the performance of the Indian economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Constitutional Provision:** According to **Article 112** of the **Constitution of India**, the President shall, in respect of every financial year, cause to be laid before both the Houses of Parliament a statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India, referred to as the **Annual Financial Statement**.
 
• **Budget Date Shift:** Until **2016**, the Union Budget was presented on the last working day of February. In **2017**, then Finance Minister **Arun Jaitley** shifted the date to **1 February** to allow for better administrative planning.
 
• **Railway Budget Merger:** Also in **2017**, based on the recommendations of the **Bibek Debroy Committee**, the 92-year-old practice of presenting a separate **Railway Budget** was discontinued, and it was merged with the Union Budget.
 
• **Digital Transition:** In **2021**, the government introduced the first-ever **paperless budget** due to the COVID-19 pandemic, where the Finance Minister read the speech from a digital tablet, a practice that has continued to promote the **Digital India** mission.
 
• **Bahi-Khata Tradition:** In **2019**, **Nirmala Sitharaman** replaced the traditional colonial-style leather briefcase with a **Bahi-Khata** (a red silk cloth folder) to carry the budget documents, signifying a shift toward Indian traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Halwa Ceremony:** This is a traditional event held at **North Block** in New Delhi, usually a few days before the budget, marking the beginning of the printing (or digital finalization) process and the "lock-in" of finance ministry officials to maintain **strict secrecy**.
 
• **Fiscal Year:** The **financial year** in India follows a cycle from **April to March**, which is different from the calendar year (January to December).
 
• **Vote on Account:** In an election year, the government usually presents an **Interim Budget** or a **Vote on Account** to meet essential expenditures until a new government is formed. Since **2025-26** is not a general election year, a **full budget** was presented.
 
• **Budget Components:** The budget is divided into two main parts: the **Revenue Budget** (short-term income and expenses) and the **Capital Budget** (long-term investments and assets).
